directions.name: Moss and Fog
directions.summary: A deep moss ground with fog-white type.
directions.curation: A dark forest pair for outdoor and land-based brands, kept muted rather than bright green.

reasoning.claim: Fog reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Moss, so the ground carries all text.
A dark muted green feels like a real landscape rather than a "green" claim. It still follows category convention.

directions.watch_out: Green is the category default for sustainability. Check how close the competitors are.
directions.choose_if: an outdoor or land-based brand wants a real landscape feel and accepts the green convention
do: Use Moss as a full ground.
avoid: Do not add a bright leaf green.

directions.name: Solar
directions.summary: Daylight white with a strong solar yellow, departing from sustainability green.
directions.curation: A deliberate departure from green: energy expressed as light, with all text in the derived dark neutral.

reasoning.claim: Solar Yellow reaches only {ratio:figure/ground} on Daylight, so it is used for fields and the mark, never text.
Yellow ties the brand to sunlight and stands apart from the green most sustainability brands use.

directions.watch_out: Yellow must never carry text on white. Every word uses the derived text color.
directions.choose_if: an energy or climate brand wants to depart from green and express light
directions.figure_role: Large fields, the mark and illustration
do: Use Solar Yellow in large fields and illustration.

directions.name: Ink Blue Studio
directions.summary: One blue family from pale wash to deep ink.
directions.curation: A single-hue studio identity: recognisable as one color without becoming loud.

reasoning.claim: Ink Blue reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Pale Blue, so a one-hue system carries all text.
One hue at two depths reads as considered and gives the work room.

directions.watch_out: A tinted ground changes how the work looks. Show work on white panels.
directions.choose_if: a studio or personal brand wants one recognisable hue without loud color
do: Show portfolio work on derived tint panels.
avoid: Do not add a second hue.
